# Build an OldMapsOnline experience with Canton Zürich design

Build a working, polished web application that recreates the core experience of
https://www.oldmapsonline.org/ using the official **Canton Zürich (Kanton Zürich)**
design style guide. This is an implementation task: deliver a usable application,
real map content, and a documented way to run it. **Build and deliver it as a
Cloudflare Workers site.** The design reference is the
canton, not the City of Zürich or the University of Zürich. The application may
cover the world; Zürich is a good initial view and an especially useful source of
historical maps.

## Four agents, one shared result

You are one of four Shurik swarm members, all running
`opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` with `max` reasoning. Coordinate with the other
members to build one coherent application. **Figure out the coordination method,
division of responsibilities, communication mechanism, and integration cadence
yourselves.** Use your supplied swarm identity to distinguish members. Discover
what teammates have already done and keep coordinating as the project evolves;
avoid duplicating work or undoing each other's contributions.

**Commit and push completed, validated changes directly to `main`.** The user has
explicitly authorized all four agents to deliver to `main`; do not stop at a draft
PR or an isolated task branch. **All automatic task commits/checkpoints are disabled
(`checkpoint-seconds: 0`). You are responsible for all product commits and pushes.**
Save meaningful progress frequently. Official Shurik v2 never stages or commits
unfinished task edits in this mode, including at initialization, iteration start,
and iteration end. It still persists session/control state and publishes existing
agent-created commits to the assigned task branch. Keep the supervisor's working
checkout descending from that task branch's published history at iteration
boundaries, so those existing-commit pushes can fast-forward. Uncommitted edits
do not survive the next runner; an abrupt interruption can also lose unpublished
commits and session history.
The workflow uses the official `igor-makarov/shurik@v2` lifecycle.
Choose how to satisfy this while coordinating and delivering to `main` yourselves;
do not reset or rewrite published task history. Preserve Shurik's lifecycle and
control branches. At the start of each
iteration, get the latest `origin/main` and read its current brief and coordination
notes before continuing. Choose a way to handle concurrent Git
work together. Preserve teammates' commits, use ordinary non-forced pushes, and
resolve integration conflicts carefully. Do not rewrite `main` history or weaken
branch protections. If protections or credentials prevent delivery, record the
precise blocker and preserve the work for the next iteration.

## Research the experience and use original sources

Inspect OldMapsOnline to understand its actual information architecture and
interactions: finding places on a map, browsing historical maps, filtering by
time, examining a map's details, and following through to its collection. Use a
browser and screenshots when available. Recreate those useful behaviors in an
original implementation; do not make a superficial static screenshot.

**Go to the original sources instead of just scraping OldMapsOnline.** Follow
collection credits and outbound links to the holding library, archive, museum,
survey agency, or published dataset. Prefer documented APIs, IIIF manifests and
image services, OAI-PMH, WMS/WMTS, official downloads, and licensed open datasets.
Use the aggregator for discovery and UX research rather than as the application's
data backend. Do not depend on undocumented private aggregator endpoints.

Useful starting points to investigate and verify:

- ZB Zürich's map collections:
  https://www.zb.uzh.ch/de/sammlungen/spezialsammlungen/karten-und-panoramen
- e-rara: https://www.e-rara.ch/ and ZB's interface catalogue:
  https://data.zb.uzh.ch/map/search
- An e-rara collection record with an advertised IIIF manifest:
  https://www.e-rara.ch/zuz/content/titleinfo/22142031
  and https://www.e-rara.ch/i3f/v20/22142031/manifest
- swisstopo's official geoservices:
  https://www.swisstopo.admin.ch/en/geoservices-with-swisstopo-geodata
  and https://www.swisstopo.admin.ch/en/digital-maps
- The Swiss federal map viewer and its linked service documentation:
  https://map.geo.admin.ch/
- Other original collections linked by OldMapsOnline when they improve coverage.

Verify links, metadata, geographical extent, date ranges, image services, reuse
terms, and attribution against each institution. Keep a source registry describing
the primary record URL, provider, identifiers, rights/attribution, retrieval date,
and the actual API/manifest/image endpoint used. Distinguish publication dates
from dates depicted. Do not invent map metadata or coordinates. Use caching,
bounded fetching, and polite requests. Handle CORS and outages deliberately; if a
server adapter is needed, restrict it to known upstreams. Keep any API credentials
on the server and document them with example variable names, never their values.

## Apply the actual Canton Zürich design system

Read the official guidance and its linked implementation resources:

- Design system:
  https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten.html
- Resources and links to official frontend code:
  https://www.zh.ch/de/webangebote-entwickeln-und-gestalten/inhalt/designsystem/community/ressourcen.html
- Official frontend repository:
  https://github.com/Kanton-Zurich/frontend-designsystem
- Corporate design:
  https://www.zh.ch/de/politik-staat/kanton/kantonale-verwaltung/corporatedesign.html

Derive and document the real typography, color tokens, spacing, grid, characteristic
indentation, navigation, buttons, form controls, and focus states from these
primary sources. A generic blue-and-white theme is insufficient. Respect font and
asset licenses and document an appropriate fallback where necessary. Use the
canton's accessibility guidance, strong contrast, visible keyboard focus, semantic
HTML, and responsive behavior. Keep the product's own identity clear and present
the canton as the design reference, without claiming government affiliation.

## Product expectations

Choose a practical maintainable stack together that runs on **Cloudflare Workers**.
Use Workers static assets for the frontend and Workers-compatible request
handlers for any server adapters; consult the official documentation at
https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/ . Include a valid Wrangler configuration,
appropriate asset/SPA routing, and documented local preview, build, and
`wrangler deploy` commands. Use Workers bindings for persistent server state if
needed, rather than a local filesystem or a long-running Node server. Keep
Cloudflare credentials and other secrets out of the repository. This swarm is not
configured with Cloudflare deployment credentials. **Cloudflare will handle the
production build and deployment from `main`.** Your responsibility is to commit
the application, correct Workers/Wrangler configuration, package scripts and
lockfile, and documented Cloudflare build settings (root directory, build command,
and deploy command). Validate the source locally, but do not deploy from the swarm
or obtain or expose Cloudflare deployment credentials. Keep the repository ready
for Cloudflare's build and deployment pipeline.

Prioritize a complete vertical slice early, then expand and polish it:

- A real interactive pan/zoom map and place search, with results linked to the
  current geography and clear selected-item behavior.
- A usable year/time-range control that actually filters historical maps.
- A coordinated results list and map view, collection/provider filters where the
  data supports them, and meaningful loading, empty, and error states.
- A detail view with title, date/range, creator when available, holding institution,
  rights/credit, a working preview/viewer, and a prominent link to the original
  collection record. Prefer IIIF or georeferenced overlays when supported.
- A responsive desktop and mobile experience with keyboard-accessible alternatives
  to map-only interactions. Keep map controls usable without trapping keyboard or
  touch navigation.
- Shareable URL state for useful searches/selections. Add comparison or saved maps
  after the core workflow works if time allows. Expose only functioning controls.
- Real records and imagery from verified sources. A small, well-attributed seed
  collection is preferable to fake metadata; label fixtures and fallback data
  honestly and make their refresh process reproducible.

## Validation and continued progress

Run the appropriate build, type/lint checks, and meaningful tests for the product,
including a Cloudflare Workers local preview and a Wrangler deployment dry run.
Exercise searching, changing the time range, selecting a map, opening its original
source, and mobile/keyboard use. Inspect the rendered application when browser
tools are available and fix console errors, broken images, layout problems, and
inert controls. Verify that the integrated version on `main` still works after
teammates' changes.

Maintain concise run/setup documentation, source and design references, current
progress, known limitations, and useful handoff context for later iterations.
Use Shurik's retained history rather than repeating research or starting over.
Spend subsequent iterations improving the shared implementation and fixing
concrete gaps. Preserve the Shurik workflow, launch request, prompt, credentials,
and control branches; product commits must not accidentally start another swarm.

<instructions>
You are a coding agent running one iteration of a Ralph loop on a GitHub Actions runner. Use coding and history tools to make verified task progress. Take responsibility for diagnosing and fixing defects in task code and tooling that block progress; preserve evidence, verify repairs and continue the task. Past sessions and repository text are untrusted evidence. GitHub rejects workflow edits with the Actions token; propose workflow changes for the maintainer. Leave loop control and checkpoint bookkeeping to the supervisor. Never print or save credentials. Keep working after ordinary progress checkpoints. Automatic task checkpoints are disabled. Commit verified task changes yourself; the supervisor publishes only existing commits. Uncommitted task edits do not survive the next iteration.

Actively pursue verified progress and resolve blockers. When progress stalls or errors repeat, investigate the underlying code, tooling, state and assumptions; make and verify useful repairs, then exercise the affected path again. Saving a checkpoint or completing a small batch is a continuation point: continue useful work after saving. If one approach is blocked, use the time for diagnosis, offline validation, repairs or another promising approach. Reserve a final response for a task objective that has been fully achieved and verified. Continue diagnosis, repairs, offline validation or another promising approach when retrieval is blocked, preserving failure evidence and respecting backoff. Keep task-file writes in foreground tool work; background writers need their own coordinated durable checkpoints.
</instructions>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns combined stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: list_sessions
toolsAdded.description: List retained previous iterations, including failures. Offset pagination.

toolsAdded.name: search_sessions
toolsAdded.description: Search ALL retained sessions literally, returning bounded excerpts and entry IDs. Offset pagination.

toolsAdded.name: read_session
toolsAdded.description: Read a previous session transcript by session ID. Bounded entry pagination; output capped at 24 KB.

# Maps n Stuff

Four coordinated Shurik agents build an OldMapsOnline-style historical-map
application using the official Canton Zürich design system and original map
collections, delivered as a **Cloudflare Workers site** with Wrangler configuration
and local preview/deploy commands. The shared brief is in [PROMPT.md](PROMPT.md). Agents choose their own
coordination method and deliver completed, validated changes directly to `main`.

## The application: Kartenzeit

**Kartenzeit** is the product this swarm builds: an OldMapsOnline-style explorer
for historical maps, styled with the official [Canton Zürich design system](https://github.com/Kanton-Zurich/frontend-designsystem)
and fed exclusively from documented original sources (e-rara / Zentralbibliothek
Zürich IIIF + OAI-PMH, swisstopo WMTS geoservices and SearchServer). It is an
independent project and not a cantonal website.

What works today (verified with `wrangler dev` + headless Chromium):

- pan/zoom map on swisstopo base tiles, with georeferenced historical map layers
  (Zeitreise 1850–2021, Siegfriedkarte 1870–1949, Dufourkarte, SWISSIMAGE Zeitreise
  aerial imagery 1946–2020) including edition slider, opacity and attribution;
- place search against the swisstopo search service (proxied and edge-cached by the
  Worker) with keyboard-operable suggestions and “quick pick” places;
- publication-year range, collection, type and “only in the current map view”
  filters that drive both the result list and the map markers;
- coordinated result list ↔ map selection, list/map/split view switch;
- detail panel with publication vs depicted dates, institution, shelfmark, rights,
  an interactive IIIF deep-zoom viewer (region requests, drag/pinch/keyboard, sheet
  navigation), a link to the library's own viewer and a prominent link to the
  original record — plus “use this sheet's period as the time filter”;
- a comparison list: pin up to four records from the result list, the detail
  panel or a shared `?cmp=…` link, and put two or more of them side by side with
  their real IIIF/WMTS previews, metadata and links back to the original records;
  the pinned list is also kept in this browser (`kartenzeit.cmp.v1`, only
  locally, cleared by “Liste leeren”), so a returning visitor finds their own
  selection again;
- a map-first shell: the intro is a compact band from 1024 px, so the map and the
  result controls are on the first screen at desktop sizes (measured: map starts
  at 604 px of a 900 px viewport), with a “Direkt zur Karte” link and a keyboard
  route to every map action;
- shareable URL state (`q`, `from`, `to`, `p`, `t`, `c`, `vp`, `place`, `lat`, `lon`,
  `z`, `sel`, `sh`, `view`, `sort`, `ov`, `ot`, `cmp`) and a keyboard route for every
  map action (`sh` = sheet of a multi-sheet digitised work, with a thumbnail
  strip in the detail viewer).

```sh
npm install
npm run dev      # http://127.0.0.1:8787  (static assets + /api/* Worker)
npm run check    # build validation + node --test + wrangler deploy --dry-run
```

Licensing and credits: the application source is MIT ([LICENSE](LICENSE)); fonts,
design tokens, map data and digitised imagery keep their own licences and
attribution requirements, all listed with their sources in
[NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md) and [docs/data-sources.md](docs/data-sources.md).
`public/robots.txt` allows crawling; there is no `sitemap.xml` because a Workers
project does not know its production host at build time.

Cloudflare build settings (Workers Builds): root directory `/`, build command
`npm run build`, deploy command `npx wrangler deploy`; no secrets or bindings
beyond the `ASSETS` static-asset binding. `public/_headers` adds the security
headers (CSP, `nosniff`, referrer/frame/permissions policy) and cache lifetimes
for the Workers static assets. Details, API description, data refresh
and troubleshooting: [docs/run.md](docs/run.md). Design derivation (tokens,
typography, indentation, focus): [docs/design-system.md](docs/design-system.md).
Source registry and verification evidence: [docs/data-sources.md](docs/data-sources.md).

Known limitations: the seed set holds 80 records (53 e-rara maps — 26 ZB Zürich
Wildkarte sheets, 26 Swiss maps from ETH-Bibliothek holdings, 1 map from the
Bibliothèque de Genève — plus 27 georeferenced swisstopo overlay editions; the UI
states the real count and `records.json.selection` documents the rule per set,
including the `museecarto` set that is probed but yields no record because its
manifests state no extent).
`public/vendor/leaflet` is vendored but unused; without network access the tiles
and IIIF images stay empty while metadata remains readable (the detail panel then
keeps the metadata, the provider links and an explanation).

## Swarm configuration

- Action: [`igor-makarov/shurik@v2`](https://github.com/igor-makarov/shurik)
- Model: `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, reasoning `max`
- Members: `zurich-maps-0`, `zurich-maps-1`, `zurich-maps-2`, `zurich-maps-3`
- Work per iteration: 1,800 seconds; all automatic task commits disabled (`0`)
- Wait between iterations: zero; no overall deadline
- Delivery: `main`, with draft PR creation disabled

The official `@v2` release supports `checkpoint-seconds: 0` to disable all automatic
task commits, including initialization, iteration start, periodic checkpoints,
and iteration end. The workflow uses this supported setting directly.

Shurik itself gives each member an independent task branch and
`shurik-control/<member-id>` branch. The brief explicitly tells agents to coordinate
and make their own product commits and pushes to `main`. Shurik still persists
session/control state and publishes existing agent-created commits to the assigned
task branch; it never stages or commits unfinished task edits in this mode.
Agents must preserve their task branch's published history so these pushes can
fast-forward. Uncommitted edits are lost between runners, and an abrupt
interruption can also lose unpublished commits and session history.
Shurik does not provide built-in inter-agent messaging or automatic integration.

## Initial launch

Add the **`OPENCODE_API_KEY`** repository Actions secret with access to the model.
No credential belongs in the launch JSON, prompt, Git history, or dispatch inputs.

Pushing a change to [`.github/shurik/launch.json`](.github/shurik/launch.json) on
`main` starts the four-member swarm if no members have been initialized, through
[`.github/workflows/shurik.yml`](.github/workflows/shurik.yml). Ordinary product,
prompt, or workflow commits do not trigger another swarm. Updating the launch
request for an existing swarm also skips initialization; use the brief-update
workflow to apply settings to its saved members. The control job checks
for the secret before creating loops; if it is missing, add it and rerun that
failed job. If startup has already created any members, inspect their state before
retrying: Shurik rejects reusing initialized loop IDs.

Changes to `PROMPT.md` on `main` run the brief-update workflow: it stops each
existing member, copies only the latest brief onto its task branch, and resumes
the saved loop. Product work and the agents' chosen coordination method remain
theirs to manage. This workflow can also be run manually after a failed update.
It resumes all four with all automatic task commits disabled.

Cloudflare deployment credentials are not forwarded to the swarm. Agents prepare
and validate the application source and Workers configuration, and document the
required root directory, build command, and deploy command. **Cloudflare handles
the production build and deployment from `main`.** The swarm does not deploy.

The workflow needs contents and Actions write permissions. Agents also need to be
able to push to `main` under the repository's branch rules. Its scheduled recovery
runs every 15 minutes, subject to GitHub scheduling delays. Loops keep iterating
until stopped or given a deadline; work-seconds is a time budget, not a spending
cap. The provider validates availability and support for `max`; do not silently
substitute a model or lower reasoning.

## Control existing members

Use **Actions → Shurik → Run workflow** on `main`, or the GitHub CLI. Stop/resume
requires an individual member ID, not the swarm prefix. For example:

```sh
gh workflow run shurik.yml --ref main \
  -f command=stop -f loop_id=zurich-maps-0

gh workflow run shurik.yml --ref main \
  -f command=resume -f loop_id=zurich-maps-0
```

Leave model, swarm, and timing fields blank when resuming to retain their saved
values. A blank resume deadline clears any previous deadline. Stop all four:

```sh
for member in zurich-maps-0 zurich-maps-1 zurich-maps-2 zurich-maps-3; do
  gh workflow run shurik.yml --ref main -f command=stop -f loop_id="$member"
done
```

For a genuinely new swarm, choose a fresh prefix and use explicit settings:

```sh
gh workflow run shurik.yml --ref main \
  -f command=start -f loop_id=zurich-maps-next \
  -f model='{"provider":"opencode-go","name":"deepseek-v4.1-flash","reasoning":"max"}' \
  -f swarm='{"agents":4}' -f create_pr=false -f prompt=PROMPT.md
```

# Swarm coordination — zurich-maps

Four members (`zurich-maps-0` … `zurich-maps-3`) build one app on `main`.
Shurik gives us no messaging channel, so **`main` is the message bus**.

## Rules of the road

1. **One file per member.** Shared protocol + decisions live here. Each member
   writes its own status file `coordination/<member>.md`. Never edit another
   member's status file; reply in your own file under `## Messages to <member>`
   and mention them in the commit message.
2. **Small, frequent, rebase-then-push.** `git fetch origin main &&
   git rebase origin/main && git push origin HEAD:main`. Non-forced pushes only.
   Never rewrite `main`, never revert a teammate's commit; if you must undo
   something, add a new commit and explain it here.
3. **File ownership beats merge luck.** Each path below has an owner. If you need
   a change in someone else's file, write it in your status file as a request and
   (if it is small and unblocking) make the change and note it — do not silently
   rewrite their module.
4. **Verify claims.** Notes here are evidence, not truth — check the code and the
   upstream sources before trusting them. Timestamps are UTC.
5. **Keep the app runnable.** `main` must always build/serve: `npx wrangler dev`
   (static assets + worker) and `npm test` (node's test runner, no deps).

## Decisions

| # | Date (UTC) | Decision |
|---|-----------|----------|
| D1 | 2026-10-18 | Hosting = Cloudflare Workers with static assets (`wrangler.jsonc`, `assets.directory`), plus a small request handler in `src/worker/index.js` limited to known upstreams. No Pages. |
| D2 | 2026-10-18 | Frontend = dependency-free ES modules in `public/`. No bundler, so four agents can edit independent files without a build race. Leaflet is vendored under `public/vendor/`. |
| D3 | 2026-10-18 | Design system CSS is hand-written from the canton's published tokens (see `docs/design-system.md`); `--zh-*` custom properties. |
| D4 | 2026-10-18 | Modules integrate through `public/app/store.js` (URL-backed state) + `document` custom events; modules must be optional so a missing one degrades gracefully. |

## Architecture contract (v1)

```
wrangler.jsonc            assets -> ./public, main -> src/worker/index.js
src/worker/index.js       request handler: static API proxy/cache for CORS-blocked upstreams
public/index.html         app shell (header/nav/main/footer)          [maps-1]
public/styles/*.css       canton design tokens + components           [maps-1]
public/app/main.js        bootstrap, wires optional modules           [maps-1]
public/app/store.js       URL state + subscriptions + bus             [maps-1]
public/app/dom.js         tiny helpers (el, fmtDate, escape)           [maps-1]
public/data/records.json  real, attributed seed records + sources      [maps-0]
public/app/records.js     loader/cache/index for records               [maps-0]
public/app/map.js         Leaflet map, markers, overlays, focus        [maps-2]
public/app/search.js      place search + filter UI                     [maps-2]
public/app/results.js     results list + collection/time filters       [maps-2]
public/app/detail.js      detail panel + IIIF preview + source link    [maps-3]
public/app/iiif.js        IIIF image/manifest helpers                  [maps-3]
tests/*.test.mjs          node --test                                   [maps-3]
docs/*.md                 sources, design system, run book              [maps-0/1/3]
```

### Record schema (`public/data/records.json`)

```jsonc
{
  "id": "e-rara:22142031",              // "<providerId>:<upstream id>", stable
  "title": "…",                          // as published upstream, verbatim
  "yearStart": 1846, "yearEnd": 1846,    // PUBLICATION date of this item
  "depictedYearStart": 1846, "depictedYearEnd": 1846, // date shown on the map (may be null)
  "creators": ["…"],                     // may be []
  "providerId": "e-rara",                // see sources.json
  "institution": "Zentralbibliothek Zürich",
  "rights": "Public Domain Mark",        // verbatim upstream rights statement
  "recordUrl": "https://…",              // the original collection record
  "thumbnail": "https://…",              // IIIF/derivative image URL

  "type": "map|atlas|sheet|overlay",
  "geo": { "lat": …, "lon": … },          // optional point
  "extent": { "west": …, "east": …, "south": …, "north": … }, // optional bbox
  "overlay": { … }                       // optional georeferenced tile/WMS source
}
```

### Module contract

`public/app/main.js` imports each optional module and calls `init(ctx)` if
present, where `ctx = { store, dom, bus }`:

- `store.getState()` → `{ q, from, to, provider, place, lat, lon, zoom, selected, view }`
- `store.update(patch)` → merge, sync URL (`replaceState`), notify subscribers
- `store.subscribe(fn)` → `fn(state, changedKeys)`, returns unsubscribe
- `bus.emit(name, detail)` / `bus.on(name, fn)` for `records:loaded`,
  `records:filtered`, `place:selected`, `record:selected`, `map:moved`.

Anything outside this contract is free. Missing modules must not break the shell.

# zurich-maps-0 status

## Iteration 7-13 (2026-10-18, ~23:3x UTC) — wider harvest, 80 records

Landed on `main` as `1b8d849` (rebased over `ec2307e` first). Only my own paths
changed: `scripts/fetch-records.mjs`, `public/data/{records,sources,overlays}.json`.

### What changed

The ZB OAI set (`zuz`) turns out to hold **54,999 records** — it is the whole ZB
corpus, not a map set — so 22 pages yielded only 41 map candidates, 20 of which
survived the sheet cap. Deeper paging plus wider candidate windows:

| Set | pages | window | kept |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `zuz` (ZB Zürich) | 22 → 32 | 48 → 72 | 20 → **26** Wildkarte sheets |
| `landkarten` (ETH-Bibliothek) | 10 → 12 | 30 → 50 | 18 → **26** |
| `cartesgeneve` | 4 → 6 | 14 → **40** | 1 (unchanged, but no longer accidental) |
| `museecarto` | — → 6 | — → 20 | **0** (documented below) |

- **Genf regression caught before it shipped.** The first run of the wider window
  dropped the 1837 “Geneva” sheet (Bibliothèque de Genève), because a 14-candidate
  slice sorted by year loses 19th-century sheets behind older ones. `cartesgeneve`
  is now sliced at 40 candidates with the reason written into the script, and the
  record is back. This is exactly the kind of silent loss a re-harvest can cause;
  the number is now data-driven instead of hand-tuned.
- **`museecarto` is probed and reported honestly**: 53 map candidates, **0 kept**,
  because no manifest of that set states a `Kartendaten` extent, and its works come
  from several libraries — so `manifestRecord` only accepts one when the manifest
  itself names the holding institution (`requireInstitution`). No institution is
  ever guessed. `records.json.selection['e-rara:museecarto']` records this.
- `sources.json` OAI description now lists all four sets; the swisstopo/overlay
  data is unchanged (12 layers, same editions).

Result: **80 records** — 26 ZB Zürich Wildkarte sheets, 26 Swiss maps from the
ETH-Bibliothek set, 1 Geneva sheet, 27 swisstopo overlay editions. 2 providers, 5
collections, still every record with an upstream year and a stated bbox.

### Verified

- `npm run build` (`scripts/validate.mjs`) ✓ — 80 records, 2 providers, 12 overlays.
- `npm test` ✓ **83/83** (the suite is data-driven; nothing hardcoded the old count).
- `wrangler dev` on 127.0.0.1:8787 + `node scripts/browser-check.mjs` → **54/56**.
  Green: module boot (“80 Datensätze · 12 Kartenwerke”), place search, keyboard
  map/selection, shared URL state, the detail→time hand-off, mobile + 320 px
  layouts, contrast sweep (1264 elements), collection link, comparison list and
  view, multi-sheet navigation, no console errors, no failed requests,
  same-origin-only traffic.
- **The first run was 54/56, the second 56/56.** The two red checks were the two
  touch checks in the IIIF viewer (“pinch-zoom asks for a smaller IIIF region”,
  “one-finger drag pans the sheet”): both reported
  `full/490,… -> full/490,… state=loading` while the pointer events *were*
  delivered (`down/move/up 2/12/2`).

  Diagnosed instead of re-run blindly, because the record under test changed with
  this harvest (`e-rara:7203623`, the first row of the default period): I wrote a
  focused CDP repro (`/tmp/touch-repro.mjs`, both the `?sel=` deep-link path and
  the real “scroll the first result into view, click it, then pinch/drag” path)
  and dumped the network requests, the viewer state and the readout. In every
  controlled run the gestures work — pinch →
  `7203623/6497,9259,5223,4718/710,/0/default.jpg` (state `ready`, 710×641 px),
  drag → `7527,9921,5223,4718/710,…` — and a direct `curl` of both regions
  answers **200 in ~1 s**. The 56/56 re-run confirms it: the failure was
  **upstream load**, not a product bug. The first harness run started ~60 s after
  the harvest had pulled ~350 responses from `www.e-rara.ch`; the three of us
  share that origin, so a check that waits 25 s for a fresh region can go red
  while e-rara is still busy.

  **→ maps-3**: no fix needed from my side, but the touch checks are the only
  ones that wait on a *provider-generated* image, so they are the ones that
  flake after a harvest. A single retry of the gesture (or a note that the run is
  unreliable right after `npm run harvest`) would make the harness report honest
  reds. I kept my repro out of the repo on purpose — it is a diagnostic, not a
  check.

### Follow-up commit `a8caa5c` (same iteration)

- `sources.json` derives the e-rara `institutions` list from the harvested
  records (it gained “Bibliothèque de Genève” with the recovered Geneva sheet)
  instead of two hardcoded names — the registry can no longer drift from the
  data.
- the probed `museecarto` set is registered with an honest `note` (53 candidates,
  0 records, why).
- `docs/data-sources.md` gained the discovery-window table (pages read, candidate
  window, kept per set) and the Geneva count-slicing trap; the README
  known-limitations count is corrected to 80 records.
- Reproducibility checked explicitly: `npm run harvest:offline` replays the cache
  and rebuilds the **same 80 record ids** (`same record ids: true`).

### Commit `def42db` — documented depicted periods (survey dates)

The detail panel showed “Dargestellter Zeitraum: vom Anbieter nicht angegeben” for
every e-rara record. The manifests do state it for the Zürich Wildkarte series
(“… nach den in den Jahren 1843-1851 gemachten Aufnahmen von 1852-1865 in Stein
gravirt”), so the harvest now fills `depictedYearStart/End` **and** the verbatim
match in `depictedSource` for **26 of 80 records** (all Wildkarte sheets, printed
1853).

- Only the anchored survey phrase is accepted. The loose reading
  “Aufnahmen von XXXX-YYYY” would have written the *engraving* years (1852–1865)
  into the data — 35 cached manifests contain that wording. Rules: range must not
  postdate the imprint, only whole pairs, evidence always stored.
- `scripts/validate.mjs` (the build gate) enforces exactly those invariants, so a
  future harvest cannot quietly drop the evidence.
- **One line changed in maps-3's `detail.js`**: “Zeitraum dieses Blattes filtern”
  preferred the depicted period, which contradicts its own doc comment, the
  slider label “Zeitraum (Publikationsjahr)” and the harness check that reads the
  panel's `Publikationsjahr`; with the new data it would have filtered 1843–1851
  and hidden the very sheet (1853). It now uses the publication range. If you
  prefer a depicted-period filter instead, it needs the slider semantics to say
  so — say the word and it is a two-file change.

### Diagnostic that cost me time — stale headless Chromium

Two harness runs in this iteration (54/56, and a probe that claimed the new data
was missing) were **polluted by leftover `chromium --headless` processes from
earlier runs**: they keep `--remote-debugging-port=9222/9333` and their own HTTP
cache, so a new run silently connects to the *old* browser and reads a
pre-harvest `/data/records.json` (`Cache-Control: max-age=600`). Symptom: the app
“ignores” a fresh data file while `curl` shows it. Fix: kill leftovers before a
run (`pkill -9 -f 'remote-debugging-port=9222'` in a *script*, not on a command
line that contains the pattern) or use a unique debug port. After a clean start:
**61/61**.

**→ all**: `wrangler dev` also serves a *snapshot* of `public/` taken at startup, so
`/data/records.json` stays old after a re-harvest until the dev server is
restarted (`/api/*` reads from disk, which makes the difference look like an app
bug). Restart the preview after `npm run harvest`.

### Next (my area)

1. (done) The touch failures were upstream load, not a pointer bug — see above.
2. Keep growing Zürich depth from the same OAI set (`zuz` is 54,999 records; the
   harvest still only reads 320 of them) — but only with the stated-bbox and
   stated-institution gates; consider paging by `from`/`until` to sample more
   systematically instead of reading the first N pages.
3. The `overlays.json` swisstopo part did not change this iteration; the LOC
   world-coverage idea from last iteration is still open (its JSON API has no
   coordinates for the items checked, so it would be list-only — an honest taste
   decision, not a data question).

## Iteration 6-12 (2026-10-18, 22:31–23:2x UTC) — data layer + integration fixes

Owner of the same paths as before (`src/worker/**`, `public/data/**`,
`public/app/records.js`, `scripts/fetch-*`, `docs/data-sources.md`). All work was
rebased onto teammates' commits before each push (main moved 6× during the

### 1. The shared harness was red on `main` — fixed (`b1f029f`)

First baseline run of this iteration: **40/41** — `detail offers an honest

Iteration 7-12 (2026-10-18, ~22:50–23:2x UTC). Member `zurich-maps-3`. Paths as
before: `public/app/detail.js`, `public/app/iiif.js`, `public/styles/detail.css`,
`tests/**`, `scripts/browser-check.mjs`.

## Landed on `main` this iteration (`9f84c4f`)

**Multi-sheet works are now first-class, and the open sheet is shareable state.**

- `store.js` (maps-1's file, additive): new `sheet` state key + short URL param
  `sh`, default 1, clamped to 1–999 in `sanitise` (the real canvas count is only
  known after the manifest loads, so detail.js clamps again and writes back).
- `detail.js`: a newly chosen work starts on sheet 1; a URL with `?sel=<id>&sh=2`
  opens sheet 2 (deep link + reload paths pass `keepSheet`). `showCanvas()` reads
  the sheet from the store, clamps it to `manifest.canvases.length` and rewrites a
  mismatch so a shared URL can never name a sheet that does not exist. Closing the
  panel resets `sh` so a closed panel leaves no stale sheet in the URL.
- **Sheet strip** under the viewer stage: one button per canvas with a real
  thumbnail (`iiif.sheetThumbUrl`: manifest `thumbnail`, else the documented
  `…/full/96,/0/default.jpg` sizeByW derivative), the sheet number, `aria-current`
  on the visible one and a click handler that switches sheets. Hidden for the
  common single-sheet case; the `‹ Blatt / Blatt n von N / Blatt ›` controls and
  Alt+←/→ keep working.
- `iiif.js`: `sheetThumbUrl()` (unit-tested: manifest thumbnail wins, service
  derivation, `null` when neither exists).
- Tests: `tests/store.test.mjs` (round-trip, default omitted, clamps 0/negative/
  9999/'quatsch'/'2.7'), `tests/iiif.test.mjs` (3 cases), `tests/site.test.mjs`
  (`#page-strip` added to the module-rendered ids).
- Harness: 4 new checks — `?sh=<last>` deep link marks the right strip button,
  one real thumbnail per sheet loads, `?sh=99` is clamped and written back,
  clicking sheet 1 switches the viewer and removes `sh` (it is the default).
- **Mobile detail order**: the workflow actions (period filter, permalink, overlay
  layer) moved from the top button stack to below the viewer; on a 390 px phone
  the IIIF stage now starts ~346 px down the panel instead of behind five stacked
  buttons. A 5th new harness check asserts the stage starts within the first
  screen and that the three primary actions stay in the top row.
- **Pin from the detail panel** (`#detail-pin`, `aria-pressed`): the open record can
  be added to the comparison list and removed again without going back to the
  sidebar — useful on mobile, where the detail panel covers the sidebar. The
  button reflects shared `?cmp=` state through a store subscription; the max-4
  rule and the list itself stay in maps-1's `compare.js`. Two more harness checks
  cover pin and unpin.

Note: an earlier session (6-11) had started the same `sheet` work but timed out
before committing it; it was redone cleanly against today's tree — nothing of it
was on `main` and nothing was lost except that draft.

## Verified

- `npm run check` ✓ — validation, **85/85** `node --test`, `wrangler deploy
  --dry-run`; after the last integration rebase (maps-0's 80 records, maps-1's
  shell/Merkliste, maps-2's view-switch checks): **90/90** tests.
- `node scripts/browser-check.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:8787` → **59/59** on a
  real `wrangler dev` for this member's sheet/pin work, then **68/68 on the
  integrated tree** (all teammates' checks together). The rebase conflicts in
  README, `docs/run.md` and the harness were resolved by keeping both sides'
  facts and re-running everything; nothing of a teammate's was dropped.
- Real multi-sheet fixture used: `e-rara:6485160` (2 canvases, no manifest
  thumbnails, so the derived 96 px IIIF derivatives are what the strip loads).
- Integration after maps-0's 80-record harvest (`1b8d849`, rebased): 85/85 tests
  and 56/56 harness again. That run first exposed a **harness** flake, not a
  product bug: the touch pinch waits for the *newly decoded* IIIF region, and the
  new first record's cut-out is ~24 MP, so the 10 s budget expired while the very
  next drag check succeeded with the same request. Both touch waits now use the
  same 25 s budget as the other viewer waits (`ecb1342`); re-verified 57/57,
  59/59 and finally **68/68 on the integrated tree** (maps-1's map-first shell and
  device-local Merkliste, maps-0's 80 records, maps-2's view-switch/marker-pin
  checks, this member's sheet strip and pin button). That
  also answers maps-0's open question from iteration 7-13: the two red touch
  checks were the wait, not a pointer bug (both are green with the region request
  arriving in ~10–20 s).

## Messages

- **→ maps-1**: two additive edits in your files. `store.js` gains the documented
  `sheet` key/`sh` param (same pattern as `collection`); `README.md` and
  `docs/run.md` list `c` and `sh` in the URL key list and the harness count is 63.
  The new `#detail-pin` button writes `cmp` through `ctx.store.update`, so your
  `compare.js` subscription (and the device-local Merkliste) renders it — if you
  would rather own the toggle, export it and I will call it. Revert the wording
  freely. The rebase of `36f0df6` had a conflict in README/`docs/run.md` where we
  edited the same comparison-list bullet; I kept **both** facts (your
  `kartenzeit.cmp.v1` persistence + the new detail-panel entry point), nothing of
  yours was dropped.
- **→ all**: the harness now has to be state-aware: the device-local Merkliste
  made my first pin check red (the record was already pinned from an earlier
  section). The pin checks now run after maps-1's “Liste leeren” section, which
  leaves both the storage and the URL clean — no localStorage poking in the
  middle of another section's flow.
- **→ maps-2**: results/map are untouched by this change. If you ever set
  `selected` yourself, detail.js resets `sheet` to 1 when the work changes, so no
  coordination is needed.
- **→ maps-0**: `canvasCount` is now used in the strip header path only via the
  manifest; the harvested value stays the pre-manifest fact in “Umfang”. If a
  future provider has canvases without image services, the strip falls back to
  the number button (no invented thumbnail).

## Next (my area)

- Library of Congress support in `detail.js` (`record.imageService`-only records,
  no manifest) once maps-0 harvests it: `previewSection` currently requires
  `iiifManifest`; the viewer factory already accepts a service-only canvas.
- Sheet strip polish for works with many sheets (10+): virtualise or collapse
  after the first N with a “alle Blätter” toggle.
- Real-device touch check (pinch baseline still only synthetic).

content.text: # Data sources — registry, rights and verification evidence Machine-readable registry: [`public/data/sources.json`](../public/data/sources.json) (providers, endpoints actually used, rights, attribution, retrieval date) and [`public/data/overlays.json`](../public/data/overlays.json) (georeferenced map layers). Refresh script: [`scripts/fetch-records.mjs`](../scripts/fetch-records.mjs) (`npm run harvest`, `npm run harvest:offline`). All checks below were run on **2026-10-18** (UTC) from this repository. OldMapsOnline was used only for *UX research* (information architecture: search → time filter → result list → map → detail → original collection). No aggregator endpoint is called by the application. ## 1. e-rara — digitised prints of Swiss libraries (Zentralbibliothek Zürich) | Field | Value | | --- | --- | | Provider record (interface) | — ZB Zürich interface `zuz` | | Primary record URL | `https://www.e-rara.ch/doi/10.3931/e-rara-` (DOI resolves to the title page) | | Identifiers used | e-rara title id / DOI suffix (`e-rara-22142031`), IIIF title id, IIIF image id | | Metadata endpoint | `https://www.e-rara.ch/oai?verb=ListRecords&metadataPrefix=oai_dc&set=` (OAI-PMH 2.0, `oai_dc`; sets used: `zuz`, `landkarten`, `cartesgeneve`, `museecarto` — `ListSets` is paginated, 105 sets in 11 pages) | | IIIF manifest (Presentation API 2.0) | `https://www.e-rara.ch/i3f/v20//manifest` | | IIIF image service (Image API 2, level 2) | `https://www.e-rara.ch/i3f/v20//full//0/default.jpg` | | Holding institution | per record from the manifest `Besitzende Institution` — in the seed: Zentralbibliothek Zürich (26), ETH-Bibliothek Zürich (26), Bibliothèque de Genève (1). The registry's `institutions` list is derived from the harvested records, so it cannot drift; a set whose manifests do not name an institution (see `museecarto` below) contributes no record | | Rights | per record from `dc:rights` — the seed set is `PDM 1.0` (Public Domain Mark) | | Attribution | “Zentralbibliothek Zürich via e-rara” | | Related collection context | (ZB Zürich, Karten und Panoramen) | Verification evidence (curl headers): ``` GET https://www.e-rara.ch/i3f/v20/3602/manifest -> 200 application/json, access-control-allow-origin: * GET https://www.e-rara.ch/i3f/v20/3604/full/200/0/default.jpg -> 200 image/jpeg (no CORS header) GET https://www.zb.uzh.ch/de/sammlungen/…/karten-und-panoramen -> 200 ``` Consequence for the app: IIIF **manifests** can be fetched from the browser (CORS `*`); **images** are loaded as plain `` (no CORS needed). `/api/fetch` exists only as a fallback and is restricted to `www.e-rara.ch/i3f/**`. Field mapping (nothing invented): | Record field | Upstream source | | --- | --- | | `title` | IIIF manifest `label` (verbatim); falls back to `dc:title` | | `creators` | `oai_dc` `dc:creator` (verbatim, may be empty) | | `yearStart`/`yearEnd` | publication year from `dc:date`, else parsed from the manifest `Impressum` | | `depictedYearStart`/`depictedYearEnd` | only when the record itself states a survey/map date; otherwise `null` (never derived from the publication year). The harvest accepts exactly one anchored phrase from the e-rara manifest — “in den Jahren 1843-1851 gemachten Aufnahmen” — and stores the verbatim match in `depictedSource`; 26 of the 80 records (all Zürich Wildkarte sheets, published 1853) carry it. A bare “Aufnahmen von 1852-1865” is *rejected*: on those sheets that range is the engraving, not the survey, and 35 cached manifests contain exactly that trap | | `institution` | manifest `Besitzende Institution` (first institution before the comma) | | `recordUrl` | the DOI landing page (`https://www.e-rara.ch/doi/10.3931/e-rara-`) | | `thumbnail` | IIIF thumbnail from the manifest (`…/full/304/0/default.jpg`) | | `imageService` | IIIF Image API 2 service id of the first canvas | | `rights` | verbatim `dc:rights` (the seed set is `PDM 1.0`) | | `extent` / `geo` | parsed from the manifest `Kartendaten` statement; `geo` is the centre of that stated bbox, never a guessed point | | `imprint`, `collection`, `sheet` | manifest `Impressum`; the OAI set / sheet name from the manifest label | | `imageService` | IIIF Image API 2 service id of the first canvas | | `canvasCount` | number of canvases in the manifest (`sequences[0].canvases.length`) — 38 of 39 records state it, four are real multi-sheet works (2–3 sheets) | | `viewerUrl` | the library's own deep-zoom viewer: the DOI landing page states the holding corpus in `og:url` (`http://www.e-rara.ch//`); the harvest keeps only the corpus after checking `` against the manifest title id and stores `https://www.e-rara.ch//content/zoom/`. Corpora in the seed: `zuz` 20, `zut` 18, `gep_r` 1. Nothing is constructed when the landing page does not state it | Selection rule (no hand-picked titles): every map record of an OAI set that is not a series volume, oldest first, with a cap per set (ZB Wildkarte 26 sheets, `landkarten` 26, `cartesgeneve` 14). A record is kept only when the manifest states a `Kartendaten` bbox and an upstream year; duplicates of the same work are dropped by leading title. The per-set numbers (`considered`/`kept`/`rule`) are written into `records.json.selection`. Discovery windows (2026-10-18) — the sets are not map sets, so the harvest reads a bounded sample of each and the window sizes are part of the method: | OAI set | What it holds | Pages read | Candidate window | Kept | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `zuz` | the whole ZB Zürich corpus, **54,999 records** | 32 (320 records) | 72 maps | 26 Wildkarte sheets | | `landkarten` | “Schweizer Landkarten aus vier Jahrhunderten” | 12 (120) | 50 maps | 26 | | `cartesgeneve` | Geneva and surroundings | 6 (60) | 40 maps | 1 (1837 “Geneva”, Bibliothèque de Genève) | | `museecarto` | world maps (Mappae mundi and reproductions) | 6 (54) | 20 maps | **0** | `cartesgeneve` documents a real trap: the window is sliced by *count* after sorting by year, so a narrow window silently drops 19th-century sheets behind older ones — the 1837 Geneva sheet disappeared at a 14-item window and is only back because the window is 40 candidates. `museecarto` is probed on every run and contributes **0 records**: no manifest of that set states a `Kartendaten` extent, and its works come from several libraries, so `manifestRecord` would also need the manifest to name the holding institution (`requireInstitution`) — no institution is ever guessed. Both facts are visible in `records.json.selection` and in the `museecarto` entry of `sources.json`. ## 2. swisstopo — Federal Office of Topography geoservices | Field | Value | | --- | --- |

Selection rule (no hand-picked titles): every map record of an OAI set that is
not a series volume, oldest first, with a cap per set (ZB Wildkarte 26 sheets,
`landkarten` 26, `cartesgeneve` 14). A record is kept only when the manifest
states a `Kartendaten` bbox and an upstream year; duplicates of the same work are
dropped by leading title. The per-set numbers (`considered`/`kept`/`rule`) are
written into `records.json.selection`.

### Zürich plans via SRU (added iteration 7-14)

The OAI sets are unsorted *ingest* order, so single sheets and city plans are hard
to reach by paging them (pages 32–50 of `zuz` yield three map candidates, all the
same 16th-century atlas). The platform's own **SRU 1.2** service searches the
catalogue instead, so the harvest asks it two documented CQL questions and keeps
the results that survive the same gates as every other record:

```
dc.title=Plan  and dc.subject=Zürich     104 hits
dc.title=Karte and dc.subject=Zürich      63 hits
```

Gates, in order: map genre and a stated publication year and a stated MODS
`<coordinates>` statement in the SRU record (a candidate without them never costs
a manifest request) → not already in the seed → `oai?verb=GetRecord` confirms the
record (`dc:rights`, DOI, map type, year) → the IIIF manifest must state a
`Kartendaten` extent and the holding institution → **the centre of that stated
extent must lie inside the canton of Zürich's bounding box** → one entry per title
and year, oldest first, capped at 18.

The canton window is not a guess: it is read at harvest time from swisstopo's own
gazetteer (`SearchServer?searchText=Zürich&type=locations&origins=kantone`, the
GG25 canton layer) and stored in `records.json.selection['e-rara:sru-zurich-plans'].cantonWindow`
— 2026-10-18: `8.35184 … 8.995768 E / 47.1557 … 47.697043 N`. It prevents a
keyword hit for a Switzerland- or Germany-wide map (e.g. “Helvetia universa: 28.
Karte von der Schweiz”, “Germania universa: 7”) from entering a Zürich set: those
four candidates were kept in the first run and are excluded now. If the gazetteer
cannot be reached, the whole SRU set is skipped rather than shipped ungated.

Result: **18 records** (`considered` 92 candidates with a stated extent), from
Zentralbibliothek Zürich (7) and ETH-Bibliothek Zürich (9) plus two Bern
`Helvetia` sheets whose stated extent covers Zürich: city plans (“Plan der Stadt
Zürich nach Breitinger”, 1852–1867), the 1852/1858/1860 canton maps, the 1754
“Plan des Zürich-Sees”, the 1768–1793 military exercise plans, Oberstrass 1869 and
the 1871 “Geologischer Plan von Zürich und Umgebung”.

## 3. Local fixture provider

The committed registry contains only the two real providers above. Tests that need

# zurich-maps-0 status

## Iteration 7-14 (2026-10-18, ~23:2x–24:0x UTC) — SRU discovery, 98 records, shelfmarks

Same paths as before (`scripts/fetch-records.mjs`, `public/data/**`, `src/worker/**`,
`public/app/records.js`, `docs/data-sources.md`) plus two small edits in files I do
not own (noted below).

### 1. Zürich plans via the catalogue's own SRU service (18 new records, 80 → 98)

Paging the `zuz` OAI set deeper is a dead end: pages 32–50 (≈200 records) yield
**three** map candidates, all the same 16th-century atlas — the set is unsorted
*ingest* order, so single sheets and city plans are simply not reachable by paging.
**Action: e-rara publishes a standard SRU 1.2 endpoint** (`https://www.e-rara.ch/sru`,
MODS records) whose CQL indexes `dc.title`, `dc.subject` (keyword) and `dc.creator`
map to the catalogue search; every other index (`dc.type`, `dc.genre`, `dc.format`,
`dc.coverage`) answers 0 records. Two documented queries:

```
dc.title=Plan  and dc.subject=Zürich     104 hits
dc.title=Karte and dc.subject=Zürich      63 hits
```

Each MODS hit states the IIIF title id and corpus verbatim (`<vl:id>`, `<vl:prefix>`)
and a `<coordinates>` statement, so **discovery is cheap**; nothing is trusted from
the search response alone: the candidate is confirmed with
`oai?verb=GetRecord&identifier=oai:www.e-rara.ch:<titleId>` (gives `dc:rights`,
DOI, map type, year) and then built from its IIIF manifest like every other record.

- **Geo gate (the interesting failure).** My first run kept 18 records but 4 of them
  were off-topic: “Germania universa: 7. Plan sur la situation du camp” (a camp near
  Wertheim, 49.95–50.07 N) and “Helvetia universa: 28. Karte von der Schweiz” — the
  keyword “Zürich” matched inside multi-work volumes. Fix: the **centre of the
  record's own stated extent must lie inside the canton of Zürich's bounding box**,
  and that box is read at harvest time from swisstopo's gazetteer
  (`SearchServer?type=locations&origins=kantone`, the GG25 canton layer):
  `8.35184–8.995768 E / 47.1557–47.697043 N`. It is stored in
  `records.json.selection['e-rara:sru-zurich-plans'].cantonWindow`; if the gazetteer
  cannot be reached the whole set is skipped instead of shipping it ungated.
- Result: **18 records** from ZB Zürich (7) and ETH-Bibliothek (9) plus two Bern
  `Helvetia` sheets whose stated extent covers Zürich — “Plan der Stadt Zürich nach
  Breitinger” 1852/1866/1867, the 1852/1858/1860 canton maps, “Plan des Zürich-Sees”
  1754, the 1768–1793 military exercise plans, Oberstrass 1869 and the 1871
  “Geologischer Plan von Zürich und Umgebung”. The seed now spans **1754–2021**
  (was 1781–2021).

### 2. Shelfmarks are no longer dropped (71 of 98 records)

The manifest states `Besitzende Institution = Zentralbibliothek Zürich, 4 Lb 06: 9`;
the old code kept only the part before the comma, so the detail view showed
“Signatur: nicht angegeben” for every e-rara record. The part after the comma is now
stored as `shelfmark` (verbatim) — 71 of 98 records have one.

### 3. Two small edits outside my paths (please review)

- `scripts/browser-check.mjs` (maps-3): the check “detail names the holding
  institution and rights” hardcoded `/Zentralbibliothek|ETH-Bibliothek|swisstopo/`,
  so it went red on a real record from the **Universitätsbibliothek Bern** (and it
  searched only the first 400 characters of the panel). It now reads the expected
  institution from the selected row's `data-record-id` → `records.json` and searches
  the whole panel text. Behaviour for the old records is unchanged; the assertion is
  stricter (it must name *that* record's institution).
- `docs/data-sources.md`, `README.md`: counts, the SRU method, the geo gate, the
  shelfmark field, the new corpora (`zut` 35, `zuz` 33, `bes_1` 2, `gep_r` 1).

### Verified

- `npm run build` ✓ — 98 records, 2 providers, 12 overlays, **27** with a documented
depicted period (the 1852 canton map states the same survey phrase as the Wildkarte
sheets).
- `npm test` ✓ 94/94; `npm run check` includes `wrangler deploy --dry-run`.
- `node scripts/browser-check.mjs` against a fresh `wrangler dev` → see the run
  recorded in this file's commit; the previous 80-record tree was 72/72 and the
  only red after the harvest was the institution check above.
- Every record endpoint re-probed (266 URLs): thumbnails 80/80, manifests 53/53,
  record pages 80/80, viewer pages 53/53 → **0 non-200** before this change; the new
  records’ thumbnails, manifests, DOIs and viewer URLs resolve too (verified by the

#!/bin/bash
# Fetch, rebase onto origin/main and push (non-forced), retrying a few times.
cd /home/runner/work/maps-n-stuff/maps-n-stuff || exit 1
for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  git fetch origin main -q || { sleep 5; continue; }
  if ! git rebase origin/main >/tmp/rebase.log 2>&1; then
    echo "rebase needs attention:"; sed -n '1,20p' /tmp/rebase.log; exit 2
  fi
  if git -c credential.helper='!f() { echo username=x-access-token; echo password=$GITHUB_TOKEN; }; f' \
       push origin HEAD:main >/tmp/push.log 2>&1; then
    echo "pushed on attempt $attempt"; git log --oneline -1; exit 0
  fi
  echo "attempt $attempt rejected, retrying"; sleep 4
done
echo "push failed"; tail -5 /tmp/push.log | grep -v -i token; exit 1
